name: Behalf.bot - Flight search and price tracking
description: Search Google Flights and monitor fares on tracked routes. Six MCP tools over the MIT-licensed `flights` package: prices on a route for a date, cheapest day across a range, register a route with a target price, poll tracked routes, list them with their price history, stop tracking. A daily heartbeat speaks up only when a fare crosses its target - or when the scraper breaks, which it reports as a failure rather than as silence.

enabled.description: Master switch. Off by default: the plugin reaches Google Flights on a schedule, which is a network egress an operator should opt into.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code requested from Google and asserted on every response. `fli` otherwise picks a currency from the caller's IP, which silently makes a price history incomparable when the install moves or a VPN changes. A response in any other currency is rejected as an error rather than recorded.

store_path.description: Tracked routes and their price history. Must sit on bind-mounted storage or every tracked route dies with the container. Written atomically (temp file plus rename), so a kill mid-write cannot corrupt it.

state_dir.description: Holds the heartbeat's once-per-day marker and the last check result. Must persist across restarts or the tracker polls Google on every 15-minute dispatcher tick.

discord_channel_id.description: Channel the heartbeat posts price alerts and scraper failures to. Install-specific, no default. Alerts go through the Discord reply tool with this id hardcoded in the call, never as terminal text - terminal relay hard-truncates at 2000 characters.

max_history_points.description: Price points kept per route before the oldest are dropped. 60 is roughly two months of daily checks.

error_repeat_days.description: How long a route that is still broken stays quiet before alerting again. The first failure always alerts. 0 re-alerts on every check, which turns a week-long Google change into a week of daily notifications; a large value risks one shout being missed and never repeated.

canary_route.description: Control route used to tell a broken scraper from an empty result, as ORIGIN-DESTINATION. It must be dense enough that an empty answer is never legitimate. When a real search comes back empty, this route is searched too: also empty means the scraper is broken and the original result means nothing.

canary_lead_days.description: How far ahead the control route is priced. Far enough out to be reliably full, near enough to be inside Google's window.

activation._note: Dormant by default. The MCP server is started on demand by the harness; the flight-watch heartbeat must be added to the install's heartbeat config at activation time, pointed at scripts/gather-flight-prices.sh with the prompt template in scheduled-tasks/. Set the cadence to daily and the criticality to background so conservation mode suppresses it - a fare alert is never worth spending a constrained budget on. The gate is free: it exits count=0 without touching a model on every tick where nothing moved, and polls Google at most once per calendar day.

system.name: python3
system.install: apt-get install python3 python3-pip (Debian) / your platform's package manager
system._explanation: Runs the tools, the MCP server and the heartbeat gate. Python 3.10 or newer, which is what the pinned `flights` release requires.

system.name: flights
system._explanation: The `flights` package (punitarani/fli, MIT, LICENSE.txt verified in the upstream repo, not inferred from the README). Pinned to an exact version, with its full transitive closure pinned in requirements.lock.txt. It is a Google Flights scraper: pinning protects an install from an upstream change arriving unannounced, it does not protect anyone from Google changing their response shape, which is what the canary in flight_tools.py exists for.

_declares._why: CONTRIBUTING.md asks a plugin to declare everything it touches, and network egress and disk paths have no dedicated manifest field. This block is documentation for an operator deciding whether to enable it.
network_egress: https://www.google.com/_/FlightsFrontendUi/... - the Google Flights frontend endpoints `flights` calls, reached on every search and on one daily heartbeat poll per tracked route, plus one control-route search whenever a result comes back empty
https://pypi.org - setup.sh only, to install the pinned dependency set
filesystem: store_path - read and written on every track / check / list / remove
state_dir - the heartbeat's day marker and the last check result
_declares.credentials: None. There is no account, no API key and no login anywhere in this plugin. Nothing is read from .env and nothing is read from Vaultwarden.
_declares.outbound_messages: Price alerts and scraper failures posted to discord_channel_id by the heartbeat. No email, no bookings, no purchases - this plugin searches and watches, it never buys anything.

_notes.one_way_only: v0.1 searches and tracks one-way itineraries. `fli` returns round trips as tuples of results with price semantics this plugin has not verified against live data, and guessing them would put a wrong number into a price history. Round trips are the next thing to add, behind a live check of what the tuple actually carries.
_notes.alert_policy: A target price is required at track time and is the only alert condition, per the default in new-jaxity#499. Alerts fire on transitions rather than states: crossing the target, dropping further below an already-alerted target, breaking, and recovering. A fare sitting below its target for a week is one alert, not seven.
_notes.failure_semantics: The plugin never reports an empty result as an answer without proving the scraper is alive. See the module docstring in scripts/flight_tools.py.
